newsitem.title: USA: S&P assigns "pi" ratings to seven Columbian banks.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns "pi" ratings to seven Columbian banks.

text.p: Standard & Poor's has assigned public information "pi" ratings to seven Columbian banks.
Among the seven banks receiving "pi" ratings, three are rated triple-B "pi", (investment grade): Banco Ganadero S.A., Banco de Bogota S.A., and Banco Industrial Colombiano S.A.
Four banks received speculative-grade ratings. Three banks were rated double-B "pi": Banco de Colombia S.A., Banco Comercial Antioqueno S.A., and Banco Popular S.A.
One bank, Bancafe S.A., was rated single-B "pi."
S&P made the rating assignments on Monday, December 16.

The seven "pi" ratings reflect S&P's view of the banking system as the second-strongest in Latin America. Continued system liberalization, recent privatization, and increased foreign participation will lead to further consolidation of the Colombian banking system, S&P said.
The rating agency said it expects competition to intensify in the short term, putting pressure on margins and thus hurting profitability.

In the medium-term, Colombian banks face several challenges, such as tightening consumer lending policies, improving asset quality indicators, and making higher investments in technology to increase operating efficiencies.

On the regulatory front, the Superintendency of Banks will need to implement consolidated supervision of offshore subsidiaries and tighten provisioning standards to solidify Colombia's bank industry risk profile relative to other systems in the region.
